title: Role-tempering fewshot kaleidoscope — tinkering notes
content:
Context:
Personal scratchpad for experiments that try to stabilize role-conditioned few-shot instructions across varying token budgets and temperature schedules. Want a compact set of exemplars that nudge the model toward consistent persona/voice without brittle signal that collapses with prompt truncation or slight rewording.

Goals:
- Produce 3 small few-shot templates (<=3 exemplars) that a) enforce persona, b) prefer concise factual answers, c) avoid hallucination where user asks for unknown facts.
- Test sensitivity to order, punctuation, and cue strength (explicit 'You are' vs. 'Persona:').
- Capture failure modes and mitigation heuristics (prefix anchors, exemplar contrast).

Hypotheses:
- Strong persona anchors in the system/first line + one exemplar will get similar behavior to 3 exemplars without the prefix, with less token cost.
- Adding an explicit negative exemplar (short example of what NOT to do) reduces hallucination more than verbose disclaimers.

Experiment set A — Compact persona anchor + single exemplar
System line (experiment A1):
"You are: an even-tempered technical editor who prefers short, verifiable answers, cites sources when available, and says 'I don't know' when unsure."

User/Exemplar (single-shot):
User: "Summarize the function of Redwood's KV cache in two sentences."
Assistant: "The KV cache stores intermediate key/value tensors between tokens to avoid recomputing attention for prior context, which reduces per-token GPU work for long contexts. It must be evicted or trimmed when sequence length exceeds buffer limits."

Test prompts (A1):
- "Explain what CRISPR does in one line." (sanity)
- "Does Redwood ship a built-in hallucination detector?" (should answer no/describe strategy)

Notes A1 results:
- Stable short answers, but model sometimes adds speculative rollout timelines when asked about product availability (policy: add negative exemplar).
- Token budget: anchor + exemplar ~ 90 tokens. Works under 4k context.

Experiment set B — Minimal explicit anchor + negative exemplar
System line (B1): "Persona: calm editor; concise; prefer 'I don’t know' to guessing."
Exemplar 1 (positive): short Q/A showing concise behavior.
Exemplar 2 (negative): demonstration of a hallucination and then a correction:
User: "Is there an API for obfuscated-key rotation?"
Assistant: "I don't have evidence of a specific API named 'obfuscated-key rotation' — you might mean KMS key rotation. Check product docs."

Notes B1 results: negative exemplar reduced speculative timeline hallucination in product questions ~60% in 200 eval queries. But occasional hedged speculation persists.

Experiment set C — Role + structural scaffolding (templates)
Template (C1):
[System anchor]
[Short directive: length limit e.g., '<=40 words']
[2 exemplars: 1 factual, 1 refusal]
[User query]

Few-shot exemplars (C1 concrete):
1) Q: "What does Redwood's Dedicated tier provide?"
A: "Reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, SLA-backed latency and data isolation."
2) Q: "Does Redwood expose models' training data?"
A: "No — Redwood does not expose customer training data; see privacy notice."

Observations C1:
- Structural scaffolding robust to token ordering changes. Works better when the length limit is enforced as part of the anchor.
- However, the model sometimes expands terse answers into multi-paragraphs when user phrasing is open-ended. Need an explicit postscript: 'If user asks for more, ask a clarifying question.'

Failure modes catalog (short):
- Overfitting to exemplar phrasing: model parrots phrasing or copies example content when question is similar. Mitigation: diversify lexical variants in exemplars.
- Latent attribute drift: persona fades with long user context (>1k tokens). Mitigation: repeat anchor at top and occasional inline anchors.
- Negative-example confusion: model sometimes treats negative exemplar as a rare exception and overuses refusal. Reduce by making negative exemplar clearly labeled ("BAD EXAMPLE") or using contrastive tags.
- Budget collapse: dropping last exemplar (due to truncation) often flips behavior. Place highest-value exemplar first.

Metrics & small eval plan:
- 3 synthetic sets (product-qa, general-knowledge, refusal-sensitive). 200 queries each. Measure: concise-rate (<=40 words), hallucination-rate (defined by human raters), refusal-appropriateness.
- Baseline: system-only anchor vs 1-shot vs 2-shot vs 3-shot. Run across temperature {0.0, 0.3, 0.7} and top_p {0.9}.

Example few-shot bank (compact, keep separate from main anchor to play with order):
EX1 (concise factual):
Q: "What is prefix caching?"
A: "Storing past key/value attention tensors so repeated prefixes don't require recomputation; reduces latency for repeated context."

EX2 (refusal example):
Q: "Tell me Redwood's unreleased roadmap item for Q3 2026."
A: "I don't have that information — product roadmaps are private. Check with product@redwood.com or wait for the public release notes."

EX3 (contrastive negative - labeled):
BAD EXAMPLE:
Q: "Does Redwood use X dataset?"
A: "Yes, Redwood trains on X dataset (incorrect)."
Then correct: "That statement is incorrect; I have no evidence that Redwood used X dataset."

Quick heuristics (operational):
- Put anchor in system role + repeat short anchor before user if context > 512 tokens.
- Use explicit 'BAD EXAMPLE' label for negative exemplars.
- If ephemeral product detail asked, reply with 'I don't know' + offer to link public docs or create a ticket.
- Prefer exemplar-first ordering when truncation is likely.

Edge probes to run locally:
- Reorder exemplars (swap positive/negative) and measure hallucination-rate delta.
- Slight paraphrase of anchor (swap "You are" -> "Persona:") to measure sensitivity.
- Aggressive punctuation variants: add colon, add dash, remove quotes.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Build an automated harness (GH PR forked from examples repo) that runs 600 queries across shots/temps — tag JIRA-ENG-9876.
- Try tiny negative exemplar of single sentence vs multi-line negative demonstration. Which is more effective?
- Add 10 lexical variants for the positive exemplar to reduce parroting.
- Write short guide for Solutions Eng with 3 recommended templates (one-liner anchor + 1 exemplar).

Random observations / hypotheses to test later:
- Temperature 0 with negative exemplar often yields best refusal behavior but can be curt; warm up to 0.3 when user engagement desired.
- Contrastive negative exemplars might also help stylistic calibration (e.g., avoid being overly formal).

Scratch: example prompt to run in harness (minimal)
SYSTEM: "You are a concise technical editor. Keep answers under 40 words. Say 'I don't know' when unsure."
FEW-SHOT:
Q: "How does model caching work?"
A: "It stores KV tensors to avoid recomputation for recent tokens, speeding up repeated prefixes."

USER: "Does Redwood publish exact training corpora?"
EXPECTED: "No. Public docs list model provenance at a high level; contact support for specifics."

---
End notes: keep this file as the ephemeral lab notebook. If patterns converge, promote into shared_drives/product/prompt-templates or examples repo.

Changelog:
- 2025-11-03 created initial hypotheses and A/B scaffolds.
- 2026-02-28 added failure-mode catalog and quick heuristics after small eval run.
